method.label: Check for a circle through the vertices

annotationRationale: Cyclicity is the central condition. Rectangle angles, equal opposite angles in parallelograms, and supplementary angles between parallel lines classify the five types.
sourceMethod: Follows the official second method, interpreting the required point as a circle center and explaining each cyclicity decision using opposite angles.

review.mathCheck: A cyclic parallelogram has equal, supplementary opposite angles, hence is a rectangle; a cyclic rhombus must therefore be a square. The isosceles trapezoid has supplementary opposite angles. Exactly the first, second and fifth types qualify, giving 3, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful expansion of official solution 6's second approach on page 3. The cyclic-angle test supplies the classification details omitted from that official paragraph; all five cases are addressed.
review.annotationCheck: Cyclicity is assessed; parallelogram, rectangle and parallel-line facts support it. The stated isosceles-trapezoid base-angle fact and rhombus classification are appropriate background.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact links support the rectangle, parallelogram and parallel-line facts. The quoted cyclic-quadrilateral link covers supplementary opposite angles; the converse also used here extends beyond its stated scope.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-C.A.3 is partial: this applies cyclic-angle facts and their converse, without proving them or constructing triangle circles; the converse is not explicit in the quoted standard. G-CO.C.11 supports opposite-angle equality, with rectangle right angles serving as background. 8.G.A.5 supports the transversal step; G-CO.C.9 overlaps through parallel-angle facts without demonstrating its proof requirements.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_255 fits the central cyclicity test, and all three support nodes are used appropriately. The supplied background facts are sufficient to reconstruct the classification.
